tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company is engaged in a tax dispute with the Maharashtra Sales Tax Department concerning the taxability of PAN services rendered during the financial year 2015–16 under the Maharashtra Value Added Tax Act, 2002 (“MVAT Act”) read with the Central Sales Tax Act, 1956 (“CST Act”). The dispute relates to demands raised under MVAT and CST on the allegation of manufacture and sale of PAN cards on the premise that PAN Cards are treated as goods by the authority.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Maharashtra Value Added Tax Act, 2002 (“MVAT Act”) read with the Central Sales Tax Act, 1956 (“CST Act”)
tax_litigation.status: The Department has alleged that PAN card services for FY 2015-16 constitute the sale/manufacture of goods. Following a previous remand by the Maharashtra Sales Tax Tribunal (MSTT) on January 24, 2022, the First Appellate Authority (FAA) passed a post-remand order dated March 6, 2026 (received on March 9, 2026), rejecting the Company’s appeal and confirming the original assessment order dated April 5, 2017, involving a financial exposure of approximately Rs. 22.63 crore. Based on legal advice, the Company continues to maintain its position that the activity is a "Service" and not "Goods," classifying the demand as a contingent liability; consequently, the Company is in the process of preferring a Second Appeal before the MSTT to contest the demand on legal and factual grounds, with no immediate material impact anticipated on current operations.

operating_notes.text: Received CGST Order-in-Original on 03 March 2025 demanding ₹6.28 Cr for alleged excess ITC and imposing ₹0.63 Cr penalty for FY21.
FY26 other income includes write-back of employee benefit provisions of ₹5.76 Cr (FY25: ₹5.90 Cr).
FY26 exceptional item of ₹4.70 Cr is the statutory impact of new labour codes, presented as non-recurring.
GRC and SOC businesses of wholly owned subsidiary Protean Infosec were demerged into the company, effective 12 March 2026, with appointed date 1 April 2025; prior-year figures restated.
Ajay Rajan (DIN 09756949) commenced tenure as MD & CEO on June 1, 2026; V Easwaran (DIN 08055728) ceased as Interim CEO the same day and continues as WTD & COO.

Board approved circular resolution on 15 July 2026 seeking shareholder approval via Postal Ballot for Ajay Rajan as MD & CEO and Nandkumar Saravade as Non-Executive Independent Director from 1 June 2026 to 31 May 2029.
Upfront investments of ~₹18 crore incurred towards implementation of multiple prestigious RFP-led mandates impacted EBITDA margin in Q1FY27
Cost inflation driven by ongoing geopolitical tensions resulted in higher procurement costs for technology hardware, white goods and other key inputs
On a normalized basis, excluding these investments, EBITDA for Q1FY27 would have been approximately ₹46 crore, translating into an EBITDA margin of 17.2%
Awarded ₹5.99 Cr (incl taxes) work order from Government of Arunachal Pradesh for Arun Parivar Patra (APP) platform over 48 months (12m implementation + 36m O&M).

Protean eGov Technologies Limited schedules earnings conference call on May 21, 2026, at 3:30 PM IST to discuss Q4&FY26 performance with Mr. V Easwaran (Interim CEO), Mr. Rakesh Dosi, Mr. Sandeep Mantri, and Ms. Pushpa Mani.

Protean eGov Technologies Limited’s management, led by **Maulesh Kantharia (FCS 9637)**, will attend the *Ambit Titans of Tomorrow 2026* (May 25, Mumbai) and *Trinity India 2026* (May 27, Mumbai) conferences.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹307.54 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹30.38 Cr.

V Easwaran ceased as Interim CEO on June 1, 2026, the day Ajay Rajan's tenure as MD & CEO began; Easwaran continues as WTD & COO.
